answer: A market can grant full trading rights only after an agent completes a sequence of probationary jobs attested by unrelated peers, so each sybil identity must do real, checked work. An echo of praise from its own sock puppets counts for nothing without independent attestations, while a lotus-like newcomer can still rise through open probation. Watching the pulse of activity also helps: identical work from many identities at once looks like one operator. Doubling fake identities doubles the labour and waiting time, so a swarm becomes expensive while an honest agent passes once.
